\begin{abstract}
We present \textsc{OntoCoDec}, a framework that translates Information Extraction (IE) ontologies into composable token-level decoding constraints.
A decidability analysis yields a two-layer architecture: a \emph{grammar layer} (context-free) compiles ontology constraints into grammars ensuring JSON validity and vocabulary membership; a \emph{semantic layer} (prefix-decidable with state) interprets type constraints at runtime via stateful token masking over a dynamic entity registry, with grammar-first fallback when constraints conflict.
% exp_ids: w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval, w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval, w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval, w5_llama_docred_lora_constrained_eval
Composed with LoRA fine-tuning on three 8B-class models across two RE datasets (up to 96 relation types), \textsc{OntoCoDec} near-eliminates domain/range violations (DR\,$<$\,0.1\%) at R-F1 41--47\%.
This enforcement introduces cross-field violations (CF) as a side effect---up to 1.18\% under greedy decoding on well-calibrated models---because per-triple enforcement cannot guarantee global entity-type consistency; beam search ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violation types at 1.54$\times$ latency.
Zero-shot evaluation reveals DR reduction of 76--99\% on SciERC and 42--90\% on DocRED, with a scale-dependent enabling dependency: neither layer achieves full DR reduction alone at 8B, while 70B semantic-only reaches 84\%.
70B-class validation on SciERC (full six-way ablation) with preliminary DocRED support, and event extraction on WikiEvents, confirm generalizability.
\end{abstract}

% Section 1: Introduction (compressed, 669→~550 words)

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Large language models are increasingly used for information extraction~\cite{li2023codeie,sainz2024gollie,wei2023zeroshot}, but when generating relation triples $(h, r, t)$, neither entity necessarily carries a type consistent with the ontology's domain/range constraints for $r$.
We call such outputs \emph{domain/range violations}: structurally valid triples that are ontologically invalid.
Violations persist across the capability spectrum: 15.4\% of triples on SciERC~\cite{luan2018scierc} and 18.5\% on DocRED~\cite{yao2019docred} under zero-shot decoding, and 0.5--2\% even after LoRA fine-tuning; rates correlate with schema restrictiveness (few valid type pairs per relation) rather than ontology or model scale.
At competitive quality (R-F1 41--47\%), even 1--2\% residual violations compound across thousands of documents into systematic knowledge graph corruption, making reliable constraint enforcement necessary.

Existing approaches leave a fundamental gap.
Schema-informed prompting reduces violations by 62\% on average but is per-relation unreliable (violations for \textsc{Evaluate-for} actually \emph{increase} by 5.8\,pp).
Grammar-constrained decoding~\cite{dong2025xgrammar,willard2023outlines,beurer-kellner2023lmql} ensures syntactic well-formedness but cannot encode cross-field semantic constraints.
Post-hoc filtering discards up to 48\% of predictions including true positives (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}).
Training-based approaches~\cite{sainz2024gollie,lu2022uie} internalize schema knowledge but provide only soft guidance without runtime enforcement.

We propose \textbf{OntoCoDec}, a framework that translates IE ontologies into composable layers of decoding-time constraints.
A decidability analysis of IE type constraints (\S\ref{sec:decidability}) yields a two-layer architecture: the \emph{grammar layer} compiles ontology constraints into context-free grammars (JSON structure, vocabulary membership) via XGrammar; the \emph{semantic layer} interprets type constraints at runtime via dynamic logit masking over an entity registry, with a scale-dependent enabling dependency: at 8B, the semantic layer achieves only 24\% independent DR reduction (near-complete when combined), while at 70B it reaches 84\% independently.
OntoCoDec compiles constraints automatically from IE ontologies, requires no constraint-specific training, and is applicable to autoregressive LMs with logits access; we validate on three English datasets (up to 96 relation types), three 8B-class models across three tokenizer families, with 70B-class validation (\S\ref{sec:70b-results}).
LoRA + greedy S1 achieves near-complete DR elimination: DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% at R-F1 41--47\% ($\pm$0.8\,pp, $+$10\% latency); beam ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violation types on both RE datasets under fine-tuning (1.54$\times$ latency).
DR enforcement converts ontologically invalid violations to individually valid but type-inconsistent ones (CF\,$\leq$\,1.4\% fine-tuned); zero-shot DR drops 42--99\% across models and datasets, with total violations decreasing $\sim$31\% (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}).

We make a systematic engineering contribution with theoretical grounding:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=2pt]
    \item A two-layer constrained decoding framework: we formalize a well-known intuition that cross-field type constraints require runtime state beyond context-free expressiveness (Proposition~1), yielding pair-based sequential enforcement at each level (\S\ref{sec:decidability}). Constraints compile automatically from IE ontologies, validated on schemas of varying restrictiveness with up to 96 relation types.
    \item A comprehensive evaluation across 3 IE datasets, 3 models (8B-class), and 2 tasks, with 70B validation (full SciERC ablation, preliminary DocRED): DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% at R-F1 41--47\%; zero-shot ablation reveals an enabling dependency (neither layer alone exceeds 24\% DR reduction at 8B; 84\% at 70B; \S\ref{sec:70b-results}); DR enforcement introduces CF as a correctable side effect (\S\ref{sec:scierc-results}); beam eliminates all violations; WikiEvents validates event extraction applicability (\S\ref{sec:wikievents}).
\end{enumerate}

[Reviewer 回复]:
[severity: warning] R21 Action Matrix 独立审查

## SYSTEMIC_ISSUE_A (Abstract CF) — MF1 方案需修正

**问题**：提议报告 CF 完整范围 0.46–12.02% 但这个范围混淆了两个截然不同的 regime：
- FT 范围：0.22–1.18%（well-calibrated models，实际部署场景）
- ZS 范围：2.55–12.02%（Llama DocRED ZS S1 是 12.02% 的来源，cross-model 表 line 41）

**建议**：Abstract 不应报告一个裸范围 0.46–12.02%。应分层报告：
- FT：CF ≤ 1.4%（已有的 bound），beam → 0
- ZS：CF 因 per-triple independent enforcement 上升（明确标注为 ZS diagnostic 的预期行为）

这样比一个大范围更有信息量，也更诚实。7 轮被标记的根因不是数字不够全，而是**叙事结构没有给 CF trade-off 正式地位**。Abstract 需要一个完整句子把 CF 作为 DR enforcement 的 acknowledged side effect，而不是在括号里塞数字。

## SYSTEMIC_ISSUE_B (Enabling dependency) — SF5 术语选择有问题

**"observed complementarity pattern" 丢失了关键信息**。当前 "enabling dependency" 捕捉了一个**非对称**结构：semantic 层依赖 grammar 层的 vocabulary normalization，反之不成立。"Complementarity" 暗示对称关系，不准确。

**建议替代术语**："empirical layer interaction" 或保留 "enabling dependency" 但统一加 "empirical" 前缀。核心修复其实是 §3 Corollary 重标签（R20 MF3 已覆盖），而不是全文换术语。

**R20 MF3 vs R21 SF5 关系**：R20 提议 Corollary → Empirical Observation（§3 标签），R21 提议全文换术语。如果 R20 MF3 尚未实施，SF5 应吸收 MF3 但保留 "enabling dependency" 这个 term，只改 §3 标签 + 加 scale qualifier。全文 24 处 find-replace 风险高（可能引入不一致），且 "enabling dependency" 本身在 §4-§5 的语境中是准确的。

## 逐条评估

### SF1 (WikiEvents)
方案 (a-c) 恰当。**不建议移至 Appendix**。WikiEvents 提供唯一的 cross-task 验证（RE→EE），且 §5.4 已标 "Preliminary"。移至 appendix 会削弱 contribution item 2 的 "2 tasks" claim。Abstract 删除 WikiEvents 具体数字 + contribution 标 preliminary 是正确的中间路线。

### SF2 (70B AWQ)
方案充分。§5.3 首次提及 70B 处加脚注 "All 70B experiments use AWQ INT4 quantization" 即可。**不需要在每个具体数字旁加 caveat**——那会让论文不可读。Limitations line 96 已有完整 disclaimer。

### SF5 adjusted R²
**不建议添加**。n=6, k=1 时 adjusted R² ≈ 0.857，数字本身 fine。但问题不在数字——是 n=6 本身不足以做回归。当前 "descriptive correlate, n=3, p=0.138" 已经是最诚实的表述。添加 adjusted R² 不会化解 "small n" 批评，反而暴露更多攻击面（reviewer 会问 residual diagnostics、influential points 等）。保持当前措辞。

### D1 (ZS 统计检验)
"greedy 确定性 + 引用 robustness tables" 方案正确。ZS greedy decoding 无随机性，不需要 error bars。在 Table 1 caption 声明即可。

### D2 (Full FT)
方案正确。Appendix L 已有数据（DR 2.74%→0%），只需在文字中更显著突出。

### D3 (核心新颖性)
同意不改。"systematic engineering contribution with theoretical grounding" 定位准确且 §7 已有。

### D4 (GoLLIE/KnowCoder)
§6 已有 GoLLIE 对比（line 14: "GoLLIE-7B eliminates DR at severe coverage cost (R-F1=0.0, 46% empty output)"）。可选加 KnowCoder positioning。

### R16 (补引用)
Text2Event + Huang et al. 合理。**DCCD/pldi2025 需核实**——这两个是 2026 年引用，确认实际发表状态（arXiv preprint vs 正式发表）。

### R17 (Figure 提升到正文)
**不可行**。MF1 已经在处理 §7 溢出到 page 9 的问题。Figure 占 ~0.3-0.4 页。在当前 page budget 下加 figure 必须同时删 ~0.4 页正文，得不偿失。建议在相关正文处加 "(Figure X in Appendix)" 引用，增强可见度但不占主文空间。

### R20 (DocRED dev set)
简单加一句，无风险。

## 回答 Director 5 个问题

**Q1 (CF 0.46–12.02% 是否足够？)**
不够。裸范围混淆 FT/ZS regime。应分层报告（见上文 SYSTEMIC_ISSUE_A 修正建议）。更精确的 abstract 表述建议：
"Under fine-tuning, DR enforcement introduces CF violations (0.22–1.18%) as a side effect of per-triple independent enforcement; beam search (k=4) eliminates all violation types at 1.54× latency. Zero-shot CF is higher (up to 12%) but decreases with model calibration."

**Q2 (70B disclaimer 充分？)**
充分。脚注 + Limitations 已有覆盖。每数字加 caveat 不可行。

**Q3 (adjusted R² self-defeating？)**
数值不 self-defeating (0.857)，但**添加是不必要的**。Small n 的正确策略是承认局限（已做），不是试图用更多统计量来增强一个不够强的信号。

**Q4 (Figure 空间？)**
不可行。Page 8 已满。

**Q5 (遗漏？)**
一处遗漏：**R20 MF3 和 R21 SF5 存在重叠**，需要统一为一个修改方案。建议：§3 Corollary → "Empirical Observation" (R20 MF3) + 全文保留 "enabling dependency" 但加 "empirical" 前缀和 "scale-dependent" qualifier (R21 SF5 精简版)。不做全文术语替换。

一处风险：SF5 全文 24 处 find-replace "enabling dependency" → "observed complementarity pattern" 在 DDL 前 48h 做，容易引入叙事不一致（每处 context 不同，不是简单 replace）。如果 Director 坚持换术语，建议逐处人工审核而非批量替换。

### R16 (补引用)
Text2Event + Huang et al. 合理。**DCCD/pldi2025 需核实**——这两个是 2026 年引用，确认实际发表状态（arXiv preprint vs 正式发表）。

### R17 (Figure 提升到正文)
**不可行**。MF1 已经在处理 §7 溢出到 page 9 的问题。Figure 占 ~0.3-0.4 页。在当前 page budget 下加 figure 必须同时删 ~0.4 页正文，得不偿失。建议在相关正文处加 "(Figure X in Appendix)" 引用，增强可见度但不占主文空间。

### R20 (DocRED dev set)
简单加一句，无风险。

**Q1 (CF 0.46–12.02% 是否足够？)**
不够。裸范围混淆 FT/ZS regime。应分层报告（见上文 SYSTEMIC_ISSUE_A 修正建议）。更精确的 abstract 表述建议：

充分。脚注 + Limitations 已有覆盖。每数字加 caveat 不可行。

**Q3 (adjusted R² self-defeating？)**
数值不 self-defeating (0.857)，但**添加是不必要的**。Small n 的正确策略是承认局限（已做），不是试图用更多统计量来增强一个不够强的信号。

**Q4 (Figure 空间？)**
不可行。Page 8 已满。

**Q5 (遗漏？)**
一处遗漏：**R20 MF3 和 R21 SF5 存在重叠**，需要统一为一个修改方案。建议：§3 Corollary → "Empirical Observation" (R20 MF3) + 全文保留 "enabling dependency" 但加 "empirical" 前缀和 "scale-dependent" qualifier (R21 SF5 精简版)。不做全文术语替换。

[Patch] R21 审稿报告综合修复。DDL 48h（May 25 ARR），所有修改必须在本轮完成。这次不用验证引用。

## 修改清单（按优先级排序）

### P0: Abstract 完整重写（合并 MF1 + SF1 + SF3 + SF4）

这是从 R15 开始反复 7 轮被标记的问题，根因是叙事结构没有给 CF trade-off 正式地位。

当前 Abstract 问题：
1. CF 选择性报告 "up to 1.18% under greedy decoding on well-calibrated models"（cherry-picking 最优情况）
2. WikiEvents 不应在 Abstract 出现（n=20 统计效力不足）
3. 12+ 数字/百分比 + 5+ 首次缩写，信息密度过高
4. DR "42–90% on DocRED" 与 Introduction "42–99% across models and datasets" 不一致

**重写要求**：
- 三段式结构：问题 → 方法 → 结果
- ≤5 个关键数字 + 定性描述
- **CF 分层报告**（核心修正）：FT regime CF ≤ 1.4%，beam → 0；ZS regime CF 更高（up to 12%）。CF 必须作为 DR enforcement 的 acknowledged structural side effect 获得**完整句子**的叙事地位，不是括号里塞数字
- 删除 WikiEvents 所有提及
- DR 范围与 Introduction 保持一致（建议统一为按数据集报告：76–99% SciERC, 42–90% DocRED）
- 减少首次出现的缩写（避免 DR、CF、RE、R-F1、LoRA 全部首次出现在 Abstract）

**Reviewer 审查的 Abstract CF 表述建议**（可参考）：
"Under fine-tuning, DR enforcement introduces cross-field inconsistencies (≤1.4%) as a side effect of per-triple independent enforcement; beam search (k=4) eliminates all violation types at 1.54× latency. Zero-shot CF is higher (up to 12%) but decreases with model calibration."

### P0: §1 Introduction 同步修改
- Contribution list item 2: WikiEvents 标注 "preliminary pilot study (n=20)"
- Line 21 "42–99% across models and datasets" 改为按数据集分报告，与 Abstract 一致

### P0: §3 Enabling dependency 修正（合并 R20-N1 + R21-SF5）
- Corollary → "Empirical Observation"
- "enabling dependency" 保留术语但全文**逐处审核**加 "empirical" 前缀 + "scale-dependent" qualifier
- **不要做批量 find-replace**，每处 context 不同需逐一判断是否需要 qualifier
- 不添加 adjusted R²（n=6 的 adjusted R² 不会化解 small n 批评，反而暴露攻击面）

### P1: 各处小改
1. **SF2 (70B AWQ)**: §5.3 首次提及 70B 处加脚注 "All 70B experiments use AWQ INT4 quantization; logit-level effects of quantization on constraint enforcement are not isolated."
2. **D1 (ZS 统计检验)**: Table 1 caption 末尾加 "Zero-shot results are deterministic (greedy decoding, temperature=0, fixed weights). Robustness evidence: cross-model variation (this table), document-level bootstrap CI (Table~31), prompt sensitivity (Table~35)."
3. **D2 (Full FT)**: Appendix L 加一句突出 "Full fine-tuning unconstrained still exhibits DR=2.74\%, which S1 eliminates (→0\%) with no F1 degradation—demonstrating constraint enforcement remains necessary even after full parameter updates."
4. **Q1 (Beam memory)**: Appendix F runtime 段落加一句 "Per-beam entity registry memory is O(|entities|) per beam; at k=8 with typical document sizes, overhead is <1MB per beam, negligible relative to model memory."
5. **Q2 (TCR in-loop)**: Appendix N TCR 段落加 "Integrating TCR into the decoding loop would require global optimization over all generated triples, conflicting with the autoregressive generation paradigm."
6. **Q3 (GCD equivalence)**: Table 16-17 caption 加 "Grammar-only results are analytically equivalent to GCD/BoostCD (same CFG enforcement; §6)."
7. **Q5 (TCR positioning)**: Appendix N 加 "TCR is complementary to OntoCoDec—it addresses CF (which OntoCoDec's per-triple enforcement cannot prevent) while OntoCoDec addresses DR (which post-hoc correction cannot guarantee)."
8. **DocRED dev set**: Limitations 加 "DocRED experiments evaluate on the development set, as test set annotations are not publicly available."
9. **§5.4 WikiEvents**: 开头加 "As a preliminary pilot study..." 定位

### P2: 补引用
- Text2Event (Lu et al., 2021, ACL) — §5.4 或 §6 event extraction 段落
- Huang et al. (2024) "Planning for Constrained LLM Generation" — §6 beam search / look-ahead 讨论
- 核实 DCCD 和 pldi2025_type_constrained_codegen 的 venue/年份是否准确

### 约束
- 主文 ≤ 8 pages（改完后 `\pagecount` 检查）
- 改完编译一次确认 0 errors
- 不要改动 Table 数据（只改文字/caption）

\begin{abstract}
Large language models for information extraction generate structurally valid but ontologically invalid triples---where entity types violate the ontology's domain/range constraints.
These violations persist across the capability spectrum and cannot be addressed by grammar-constrained decoding (which lacks cross-field type awareness) or post-hoc filtering (which discards valid predictions).

We present \textsc{OntoCoDec}, a framework that compiles information extraction ontologies into composable token-level decoding constraints.
A decidability analysis shows that domain/range constraints exceed context-free expressiveness, yielding a two-layer architecture: a grammar layer enforces structural validity and vocabulary membership; a semantic layer enforces type constraints at runtime through stateful masking over a dynamic entity registry, with grammar-first fallback when constraints conflict.

% exp_ids: w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval, w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval, w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval, w5_llama_docred_lora_constrained_eval
Composed with LoRA fine-tuning across three 8B-class models and two relation extraction datasets (up to 96 relations), \textsc{OntoCoDec} near-eliminates domain/range violations ($<$\,0.1\%) at F1 41--47\%.
Under fine-tuning, this enforcement introduces cross-field type inconsistencies ($\leq$1.4\%) as a side effect of per-triple independent enforcement; beam search ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violation types at 1.54$\times$ latency.
In zero-shot settings, cross-field rates are higher (up to 12\%) but decrease with model calibration.
Zero-shot domain/range reductions span 76--99\% on SciERC and 42--90\% on DocRED, with a scale-dependent empirical relationship between the two layers: the semantic layer alone achieves substantially stronger reduction at larger model scale.
\end{abstract}

We propose \textbf{OntoCoDec}, a framework that translates IE ontologies into composable layers of decoding-time constraints.
A decidability analysis of IE type constraints (\S\ref{sec:decidability}) yields a two-layer architecture: the \emph{grammar layer} compiles ontology constraints into context-free grammars (JSON structure, vocabulary membership) via XGrammar; the \emph{semantic layer} interprets type constraints at runtime via dynamic logit masking over an entity registry, with a scale-dependent enabling dependency: at 8B, the semantic layer achieves only 24\% independent DR reduction (near-complete when combined), while at 70B it reaches 84\% independently.
OntoCoDec compiles constraints automatically from IE ontologies, requires no constraint-specific training, and is applicable to autoregressive LMs with logits access; we validate on three English datasets (up to 96 relation types), three 8B-class models across three tokenizer families, with 70B-class validation (\S\ref{sec:70b-results}).
LoRA + greedy S1 achieves near-complete DR elimination: DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% at R-F1 41--47\% ($\pm$0.8\,pp, $+$10\% latency); beam ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violation types on both RE datasets under fine-tuning (1.54$\times$ latency).
DR enforcement converts ontologically invalid violations to individually valid but type-inconsistent ones (CF\,$\leq$\,1.4\% fine-tuned); zero-shot DR drops 76--99\% on SciERC and 42--90\% on DocRED, with total violations decreasing $\sim$31\% (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}).

We make a systematic engineering contribution with theoretical grounding:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=2pt]
    \item A two-layer constrained decoding framework: we formalize a well-known intuition that cross-field type constraints require runtime state beyond context-free expressiveness (Proposition~1), yielding pair-based sequential enforcement at each level (\S\ref{sec:decidability}). Constraints compile automatically from IE ontologies, validated on schemas of varying restrictiveness with up to 96 relation types.
    \item A comprehensive evaluation across 3 IE datasets, 3 models (8B-class), and 2 tasks, with 70B validation (full SciERC ablation, preliminary DocRED): DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% at R-F1 41--47\%; zero-shot ablation reveals an empirical enabling dependency (neither layer alone exceeds 24\% DR reduction at 8B; 84\% at 70B; \S\ref{sec:70b-results}); DR enforcement introduces CF as a correctable side effect (\S\ref{sec:scierc-results}); beam eliminates all violations; a preliminary pilot study on WikiEvents (n${=}$20 test documents) validates event extraction applicability (\S\ref{sec:wikievents}).
\end{enumerate}

% Section 1: Introduction (compressed, 669→~550 words)

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Large language models are increasingly used for information extraction~\cite{li2023codeie,sainz2024gollie,wei2023zeroshot}, but when generating relation triples $(h, r, t)$, neither entity necessarily carries a type consistent with the ontology's domain/range constraints for $r$.
We call such outputs \emph{domain/range violations}: structurally valid triples that are ontologically invalid.
Violations persist across the capability spectrum: 15.4\% of triples on SciERC~\cite{luan2018scierc} and 18.5\% on DocRED~\cite{yao2019docred} under zero-shot decoding, and 0.5--2\% even after LoRA fine-tuning; rates correlate with schema restrictiveness (few valid type pairs per relation) rather than ontology or model scale.
At competitive quality (R-F1 41--47\%), even 1--2\% residual violations compound across thousands of documents into systematic knowledge graph corruption, making reliable constraint enforcement necessary.

Existing approaches leave a fundamental gap.
Schema-informed prompting reduces violations by 62\% on average but is per-relation unreliable (violations for \textsc{Evaluate-for} actually \emph{increase} by 5.8\,pp).
Grammar-constrained decoding~\cite{dong2025xgrammar,willard2023outlines,beurer-kellner2023lmql} ensures syntactic well-formedness but cannot encode cross-field semantic constraints.
Post-hoc filtering discards up to 48\% of predictions including true positives (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}).
Training-based approaches~\cite{sainz2024gollie,lu2022uie} internalize schema knowledge but provide only soft guidance without runtime enforcement.

We propose \textbf{OntoCoDec}, a framework that translates IE ontologies into composable layers of decoding-time constraints.
A decidability analysis of IE type constraints (\S\ref{sec:decidability}) yields a two-layer architecture: the \emph{grammar layer} compiles ontology constraints into context-free grammars (JSON structure, vocabulary membership) via XGrammar; the \emph{semantic layer} interprets type constraints at runtime via dynamic logit masking over an entity registry, with a scale-dependent enabling dependency: at 8B, the semantic layer achieves only 24\% independent DR reduction (near-complete when combined), while at 70B it reaches 84\% independently.
OntoCoDec compiles constraints automatically from IE ontologies, requires no constraint-specific training, and is applicable to autoregressive LMs with logits access; we validate on three English datasets (up to 96 relation types), three 8B-class models across three tokenizer families, with 70B-class validation (\S\ref{sec:70b-results}).
LoRA + greedy S1 achieves near-complete DR elimination: DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% at R-F1 41--47\% ($\pm$0.8\,pp, $+$10\% latency); beam ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violation types on both RE datasets under fine-tuning (1.54$\times$ latency).
DR enforcement converts ontologically invalid violations to individually valid but type-inconsistent ones (CF\,$\leq$\,1.4\% fine-tuned); zero-shot DR drops 76--99\% on SciERC and 42--90\% on DocRED, with total violations decreasing $\sim$31\% (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}).

We make a systematic engineering contribution with theoretical grounding:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=2pt]
    \item A two-layer constrained decoding framework: we formalize a well-known intuition that cross-field type constraints require runtime state beyond context-free expressiveness (Proposition~1), yielding pair-based sequential enforcement at each level (\S\ref{sec:decidability}). Constraints compile automatically from IE ontologies, validated on schemas of varying restrictiveness with up to 96 relation types.
    \item A comprehensive evaluation across 3 IE datasets, 3 models (8B-class), and 2 tasks, with 70B validation (full SciERC ablation, preliminary DocRED): DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% at R-F1 41--47\%; zero-shot ablation reveals an empirical enabling dependency (neither layer alone exceeds 24\% DR reduction at 8B; 84\% at 70B; \S\ref{sec:70b-results}); DR enforcement introduces CF as a correctable side effect (\S\ref{sec:scierc-results}); beam eliminates all violations; a preliminary pilot study on WikiEvents (n${=}$20 test documents) validates event extraction applicability (\S\ref{sec:wikievents}).
\end{enumerate}
